battle.title: Status Code Roulette
battle.description: Methods, status codes and the padlock: spin the HTTP wheel.

questions.text: What does the HTTP status code 404 mean?
options: The server crashed while handling the request
The requested resource was not found
The client must log in first
questions.answer: The requested resource was not found
questions.explanation: 404 is a client error (4xx) saying the server could not find the resource. A crash is 500, a missing login is 401, and a permanent move is 301.

questions.text: Which class of HTTP status codes signals a server-side error?
questions.explanation: 5xx means the server failed on a valid request (500, 502, 503). 4xx means the client sent something wrong, 3xx are redirections and 2xx are successes.

questions.text: A web form must submit a new order that creates a record on the server. Which method is appropriate?
questions.explanation: POST sends data in the body to create or process something. GET is for safe reads and puts parameters in the URL, so it must not change server state.

questions.text: What does HTTPS add on top of plain HTTP?
options: Hiding the client and server IP addresses from the network
Protection against bugs in the server application
TLS encryption, integrity checks and server authentication
questions.answer: TLS encryption, integrity checks and server authentication
questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS: it encrypts the traffic, detects tampering and proves the server's identity via a certificate. IP addresses remain visible and the server code is as vulnerable as before.

questions.text: Which request is idempotent, meaning that sending it twice leaves the server in the same state as sending it once?
options: PUT /users/7 with a full replacement body
questions.answer: PUT /users/7 with a full replacement body
questions.explanation: Replacing a resource with the same full body twice gives the same result. Each POST creates another record, and a PATCH that increments changes state every time.
